assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms) opened a route to fractional frequency uncertainties near 1e-18, redefining precision timekeeping and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and searches for dark-sector physics. The idea is original, the experimental demonstration unambiguous, and the instrument-level achievement is of the kind I value as an experimentalist.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first strontium lattice clock; Ye's group then drove the record accuracy and stability and the many-body clock work. A two-person prize is a fair configuration, though the earlier ion-clock and optical-frequency-comb work, already recognised, and other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow and colleagues) contribute to the field's maturity.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide across Sr, Yb and other species, with clock comparisons that agree at the 1e-18 level; the 2026 timing is mature and the redefinition of the second is under discussion.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to separate the original magic-wavelength proposal from later accuracy records and from the 2005 comb prize contribution.
I cannot independently verify exact current record uncertainties; stated from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a large theta-13 via reactor antineutrino disappearance completed the three-flavour mixing picture and made leptonic CP violation experimentally accessible, shaping the whole next-generation neutrino programme (DUNE, Hyper-K, JUNO). It was a decisive, precise and clean measurement with a clear scientific question.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) announced in 2012, following a Double Chooz indication and T2K appearance hints; the three named people are the project leaders, but Double Chooz is not represented in the credited names and the credit is inherently collaborative. Spokesperson-based attribution is defensible but not free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple reactor experiments and accelerator measurements, with consistent precision improvements through a decade of data-taking; interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Fair treatment of Double Chooz and the accelerator results is unresolved.
Large-collaboration credit to three individuals may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos beyond 100 TeV opened neutrino astronomy; subsequent evidence for the blazar TXS 0506+056 and for neutrinos from the Galactic plane gives the discovery real astrophysical content. The instrument concept, a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov array in Antarctic ice, is original and audacious, and is squarely in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its AMANDA predecessor; a single laureate is a coherent configuration, though a large collaboration and early ideas (e.g. Markov, DUMAND pioneers, Learned) share the underlying credit, and the supplied credit lists only one name. As an astroparticle physicist I note the field proximity but know of no recorded conflict.
assessment.maturity: Independently supported by ANTARES and KM3NeT hints and by multiple analysis channels; the origin of the diffuse flux is not yet fully resolved, but the discovery of the flux itself is firm.
uncertainties: Sources of most of the diffuse flux remain unidentified, which could make the physics story seem incomplete.
Single-name attribution omits other founding leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provided the architecture for superconducting quantum processors, with strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons, dispersive readout and the transmon platform; it underlies today's leading quantum-computing hardware and quantum-optics experiments on a chip.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators provided the theory proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first strong-coupling demonstrations and later engineering; Girvin's theoretical role is also decisive, so selection of three from four is a real tradeoff. The transmon inventors are separate from this list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across dozens of groups and now an industrial platform; however the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely related, so timing and overlap require care.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may reduce room for a related award.
Allocation among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the seed fluctuations of cosmic structure, and its generic predictions (near scale-invariant adiabatic perturbations, a slight red tilt) have been confirmed to high precision by COBE, WMAP and Planck data. It is among the most consequential ideas in modern cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario and the horizon/flatness motivation, Linde the new and chaotic inflation that make it work, Mukhanov the quantum origin of structure; Starobinsky's earlier contribution is a well known omission and he is deceased, which complicates a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Observationally supported but not decisively verified; the primordial gravitational-wave signature is not detected, and alternative models remain, so a prize for the specific mechanism could be seen as premature.
uncertainties: Absence of primordial B-mode detection leaves inflation as a paradigm rather than a verified mechanism.
Starobinsky's priority and the Soviet/Western split of credit remain unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation created a leading quantum-computing platform with the highest-fidelity gates and long coherence, and fed directly into quantum simulation and metrology.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller wrote the 1995 proposal; experimental demonstrations came from the Wineland group (already recognised in 2012) and from Blatt's Innsbruck group, which carried out the controlled entangling gates and scalable operations. Including Blatt makes the configuration experiment-plus-theory; Wineland's earlier prize reduces but does not remove the need to recognise the later Innsbruck work.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many groups and companies; mature and still developing, with strong independence of replication.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and with the optical-lattice candidate on the Cirac and Zoller names.
Whether Blatt or other experimental leaders (e.g. Monroe) are the better partner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of magic-angle flat bands and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire quantum-materials field with a large impact on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the decisive experiments; the configuration is natural, though Cao and others in the experimental group and earlier theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) are part of the history.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with numerous extensions, but the physics of the superconducting pairing remains debated and the field is still young, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
Prior theory credit and junior experimental contributors are not included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first full-sky high-precision CMB maps, fixing cosmological parameters to percent level, establishing the Lambda-CDM model and confirming the flat geometry and age of the Universe; it is a landmark satellite instrument and analysis effort.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as PI, Page contributed to the instrument design and calibration, and Spergel to the cosmological interpretation; credit is shared with a large team and with COBE, already awarded in 2006, and with Planck, which supersedes WMAP in precision.
assessment.maturity: Results have been repeatedly confirmed by Planck and ground-based experiments, so the maturity is high, but the scientific novelty relative to the COBE and 2019 cosmology awards is arguable.
uncertainties: Closeness to prior cosmology prizes may weigh against a new award.
Planck and other team leaders are not in the credited names.
